title: Texas countryclubs, a broke return and a Tulsa engagement
summary: Booking agents leave them unpaid in Dallas, they reach Corpus Christi, then take cabs to a Tulsa ballroom paying a few dollars a night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: We played through Oklahoma, we even played church concerts. To no avail. And things were really tough. We played towns like Seminole. Many small towns. It was just rough. So we changed booking agents and I can't think of the booking agent we secured, but he decided to book us into Dallas and to play some dates at the countryclubs and what-not and this we did. So we left -- we had left Oklahoma and we had gone to Arkansas and played around through Missouri and different places and we went through Kansas City on our way back to Texas.

We played at a big countryclub in Dallas, Texas. I remember that. New Year's eve, 1931. We played Adolphus Hotel, for a big affair, but we never did get the money we were supposed to get. I don't know whether the booking agents were taking the money or what. But we never got what we were supposed to get, all we got was just a little hand-out, maybe $3.00 or $4.00. Four or five dollars a man.

So we strung up out through Texas, we hung around San Antonio, and also Austin, Texas. And, finally, we went out to Corpus Christi, Texas. You can't go no further than Corpus Christi, cause that's way out there on the Gulf. And the owners of two ballrooms in Tulsa, sent us a telegram, offering us a six-weeks engagement to come to Tulsa to play at this particular ballroom.
So we had to get some cab drivers to drive us to

Tulsa. We got to Tulsa and we got advanced money, that paid for the cab drivers so the cab drivers could go back to Corpus Christi. And we played this particular ballroom and the best we could make would be four and five dollars a night. And by the time you got through paying for your expenses, working about three nights a week, you didn't have much left. So we wound up in Oklahoma City at the Ritz Ballroom.
